mainTopic: Medical advice in the גמרא: remedies, causes of illness, healthy eating, marital relations, and lists of things that weaken or harm the body
overview: This amud of גיטין continues a long run of medical advice and folk remedies. It finishes one remedy, gives a cure for the skin disease חזזיתא, and describes two deadly injuries where treatment can only buy the person time to instruct his household. Next comes the illness אחילו: what causes it (even overeating dates), what it is (a 'fire of the bones'), and a detailed treatment routine from אביי's mother. The גמרא then gives general health advice: אליהו's rule to eat a third, drink a third and leave a third empty, רבי חייא's tips for digestion, and warnings about cheap white wine and other causes of weakness. A section follows on times and ways of marital relations that can harm the children or the man himself, with a remedy for דלריא and a strengthening drink that רבי יוחנן praises. The amud ends with numbered lists: things that weaken a person, things that harm the body, things that bring a person close to death or kill him, things good only in small amounts, and things that reduce fertility. It closes as רב פפא begins a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the previous remedy: palm-trellised grapes in water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes a remedy whose beginning appeared just before this section. The last ingredient is grapes from a vine grown on a palm tree, soaked in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grapes of a palm-trellised vine, in water.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line is the tail end of a remedy that started before this section. It names the final ingredient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new topic starts here. The גמרא is still in the middle of its list of cures, and this line closes off the previous recipe before the next one begins.

keyTerms.meaning: a palm tree (here, grapes from a vine grown up a palm tree)

phrases.english: Grapes of a palm-trellised vine, in water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a remedy begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The previous remedy ends with grapes from a palm-trellised vine soaked in water.

steps.title: A remedy for the skin disease חזזיתא
steps.stepSummary: For חזזיתא, a skin disease, one roasts seven large wheat kernels on a new hoe. Then one draws out their oil and rubs it on the skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: For חזזיתא: let him bring seven large wheat kernels and roast them on a new hoe. Oil will come out of them, and he should rub it on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new remedy, this time for a skin disease called חזזיתא. It gives a step-by-step recipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The recipe has three parts: take seven large wheat kernels, roast them on the blade of a new hoe, then rub the oil that comes out onto the skin. The hoe must be new, probably so that it is clean.

keyTerms.meaning: a skin disease (a kind of rash or lichen)

phrases.english: For lichen (a skin disease):
let him bring seven large wheat kernels,
and roast them on a new hoe,
and oil will come out of them, and he should rub it on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new remedy in the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil from seven large wheat kernels roasted on a new hoe, rubbed onto the skin, treats חזזיתא.

steps.title: A story showing the wheat-oil remedy works
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי used this remedy on a non-Jew with a serious skin disease, and the man was healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי made it for a certain non-Jew who had 'something else,' and he was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to show that the remedy really works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story goes further than the original recipe. The remedy healed even 'something else,' a polite way of saying צרעת, which is more serious than חזזיתא. The story shows how strong the cure is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'something else,' a polite way of naming an unpleasant disease (here, צרעת)

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי עֲבַד לֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi made it
for a certain gentile who had 'something else,' and he was healed.
phrases.notes: 'Something else' is a polite way of saying צרעת, so the גמרא doesn't have to name the disease.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי עֲבַד לֵיהּ לְהָהוּא גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the remedy from step 2 with a real case
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב שימי בר אשי healed a non-Jew who had צרעת using it

steps.title: שמואל: keeping a man wounded by Persian spears alive a little longer
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that a person wounded by Persian spears will not survive. Feeding him fatty roasted meat and undiluted wine may keep him alive long enough to instruct his household.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Someone struck by Persian spears will not live. In the meantime, let them feed him fatty meat roasted on coals, and undiluted wine. Perhaps he will live a little and instruct his household.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל describes a deadly wound and gives a way to buy the injured person a little more time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a cure, because שמואל says plainly that the man will die. The goal of the fatty meat and strong wine is only to give him a short time to tell his family his final wishes.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a remedy that saves his life. שמואל only hopes to keep him alive 'a little' longer, so he can settle his affairs.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One whom they struck
with Persian spears,
will certainly not live;
in the meantime, let them feed him
fatty meat roasted on coals, and undiluted wine;
perhaps he will live a little and instruct his household.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַאי מַאן דִּמְחוֹ לֵיהּ בַּאֲלוֹנְכֵּי דְפָרְסָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from cures to measures that only delay a certain death
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Persian spear wound is fatal, but fatty roasted meat and undiluted wine may extend life briefly so the person can give final instructions.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין: someone who swallowed a hornet
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין gives a parallel case. A person who swallowed a hornet will not survive, but a רביעית of sharp vinegar may keep him alive long enough to instruct his household.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: Someone who swallowed a hornet will not live. In the meantime, let them give him a quarter-לוג of sharp vinegar to drink. Perhaps he will live a little and instruct his household.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין gives a second deadly case that follows the same pattern as שמואל's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording matches שמואל's statement almost word for word: he will not live, in the meantime do this, perhaps he will live a little. Only the injury and the treatment change. Here it is a swallowed hornet, treated with a measured amount of sharp vinegar.

keyTerms.meaning: a רביעית, a quarter of a לוג

steps.whatToRemember: Both שמואל and רב אידי בר אבין follow the same pattern. Some injuries cannot be cured, but a treatment can buy a little time so the person can give final instructions to his family.

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
One who swallowed a hornet
will certainly not live;
in the meantime, let them give him to drink
a quarter of sharp vinegar;
phrases.notes: A רביעית is a quarter of a לוג, a common measure of liquid.

phrases.english: perhaps he will live a little and instruct his household.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין: הַאי מַאן דִּבְלַע זִיבּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case with the same structure as שמואל's statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swallowing a hornet is fatal, but a רביעית of sharp vinegar may extend life briefly so the person can give final instructions.

steps.title: What brings on the illness אחילו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says that eating ox meat with turnip and then sleeping in the full moonlight in summer brings on אחילו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: if someone ate ox meat with turnip, and then slept in the moonlight on the 14th or 15th night of the month during the summer season, he gets sick with אחילו.
steps.whatsHappening: A new medical teaching begins. רבי יהושע בן לוי lists a set of conditions that together bring on a disease called אחילו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the conditions are listed together: a specific food pairing, sleeping under the moon, nights when the moon is full, and the summer season. The name of the disease is given here, but the גמרא only explains what it is later, in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of a serious illness, a kind of fever

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
If one ate ox meat with a turnip,
and slept in the moonlight

phrases.aramaic: בְּלֵילֵי אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר אוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר
phrases.english: on the nights of the fourteenth or the fifteenth
in the season of Tammuz,
he will be seized by אחילו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of medical teachings, this time naming a new illness and what causes it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ox meat with turnip, followed by sleeping in the full moonlight in summer, brings on אחילו.

steps.title: Overeating also brings on אחילו
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds another cause: anyone who stuffs himself with any food can get אחילו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: and someone who fills his stomach with any food also gets sick with אחילו.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a second cause of the same illness: eating too much of anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first cause in step 6 was a narrow, specific set of conditions. This one is very broad. Overeating any food at all can bring on אחילו.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: And one who fills his stomach with anything,
will be seized by אחילו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, broader cause of the illness from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Filling one's stomach with any food brings on אחילו.

steps.title: Even overeating dates
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the rule about overeating applies even to dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: even if he stuffed himself with dates.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds that overeating dates also counts. In the next two steps the גמרא asks why he needed to say this, and then answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dates are singled out for a reason, but רב פפא does not give it here. The גמרא will ask in step 9 why he needed to say this at all.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Even from dates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's rule to one specific food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Overeating dates also brings on אחילו.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say this, since the ברייתא already said 'any food.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: the ברייתא already said 'anything', so dates are obviously included. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that a teaching should add something new. If 'anything' already covers dates, רב פפא seems to be saying nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! Why say it?

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב פפא's statement in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's statement that overeating dates also causes אחילו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already said 'anything', which includes dates, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Dates are healthy, but not in excess
steps.stepSummary: Because dates were praised as very healthy, one might think they could never cause harm. רב פפא teaches that they can.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since the Master said that dates fill you up, warm you, loosen the bowels, strengthen you, and do not weaken you, I would say that overeating them does not cause harm. So רב פפא teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Dates have a known reputation as a healthy food, so we needed רב פפא to tell us that too many of them can still make you sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רב פפא, someone could think dates are an exception to the 'anything' rule, because they are so good for the body. רב פפא closes that door: even a healthy food causes אחילו when eaten in excess.
steps.whatToRemember: Even a food known to be healthy, like dates, causes harm when a person stuffs himself with it.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say,
since the Master said:
Dates satisfy and warm the body,
act as a laxative, strengthen, and do not weaken;
I would say that they do not cause harm,
so he teaches us that they do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains what new point the statement adds (a 'you might have thought' answer)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since dates are praised as healthy, overeating them might be harmless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even dates cause אחילו when eaten in excess.

steps.title: What is אחילו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the illness אחילו is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is אחילו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the word אחילו means. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The illness has been named twice now, but it has not been described. The גמרא asks for a definition.

phrases.english: What is אחילו?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the causes of the illness to the meaning of its name.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term אחילו.

steps.title: A fire of the bones
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that אחילו is a 'fire of the bones.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: it is a fire of the bones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that אחילו is a burning fever felt in the bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer is in Hebrew, 'אש של עצמות'. The גמרא will ask about these words too, in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Fire of the bones, a burning fever

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵשׁ שֶׁל עֲצָמוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: A fire of the bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵשׁ שֶׁל עֲצָמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחילו is a 'fire of the bones.'

steps.title: What is a fire of the bones?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר's phrase 'fire of the bones' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a 'fire of the bones'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clearer explanation of רבי אלעזר's words. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after רבי אלעזר's answer, the גמרא wants the everyday name of the illness that people would recognize.

phrases.english: What is a 'fire of the bones'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a clearer explanation of the answer in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The everyday name for 'fire of the bones.'

steps.title: The common name: אש גרמי
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the Aramaic name people used for the illness.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is what people call 'אש גרמי.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that this is the illness known in Aramaic as אש גרמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not give new medical details. He links the Hebrew phrase to the name people used in everyday speech, so everyone would know which illness was meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Aramaic for 'bone fire', the everyday name of the illness

phrases.english: Abaye said: Esh garmei.
phrases.notes: אביי says the illness's name in Aramaic: גרמי means bones. This was the name people used for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the illness commonly called אש גרמי.

steps.title: What is the cure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how אחילו is treated.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is its cure?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the illness has been defined, the גמרא asks for its remedy. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion moves from causes, to definition, to treatment.

phrases.english: What is its remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the illness to asking how to treat it.

steps.title: Drink the medicine until healed
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes his mother: most medicinal drinks are taken for 3, 7, or 12 days, but this one is taken until the person is cured.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me that all medicinal drinks are taken for three, seven, or twelve days. But this one is taken until the person is healed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the treatment rule he learned from his mother. Unlike other medicinal drinks, the drink for אחילו has no set number of days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other medicinal drinks have a fixed course of 3, 7, or 12 days. The treatment for אחילו is different: it continues for as long as needed, until the illness is gone.
steps.whatToRemember: אחילו is caused by certain conditions and by overeating, even of healthy dates. It is a 'fire of the bones', and its drink is taken until the person is fully healed.

phrases.english: Abaye said: My mother told me:
phrases.notes: This is אביי's foster mother. He often quotes her medical advice.

phrases.english: All medicinal drinks are taken for
three, or seven, or twelve days;
but this one is taken until he is healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Unlike other drinks with fixed courses, the drink for אחילו is taken until the person is healed.

steps.title: The medicine for אחילו is taken after a meal
steps.stepSummary: אביי's mother continues: most medicinal drinks are taken on an empty stomach, but this one is taken after eating, drinking, using the bathroom and washing hands. It is a mix of lentil שתיתא and aged wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: All medicinal drinks are taken on an empty stomach. But this one is taken after he eats, drinks, goes to the bathroom, comes out and washes his hands. Then they bring him a handful of lentil שתיתא and a handful of aged wine. He mixes them together and eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues אביי's mother's instructions for treating אחילו. It shows another way this medicine is different from other medicines, and then gives the recipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 she said this drink is different because it is taken until the person is cured. Now she adds a second difference: other drinks are taken on an empty stomach, but this one is taken right after a full routine of eating and using the bathroom. Then she lists the two ingredients and how to prepare them.

keyTerms.meaning: On an empty stomach (literally, 'on an empty heart')
A food mixture, here made from lentils

phrases.english: All medicinal drinks are taken on an empty heart,
phrases.notes: 'Empty heart' means an empty stomach, before eating anything.

phrases.english: but this one is taken after he eats and drinks,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the medicine for אחילו from the previous step.

phrases.english: and goes into the bathroom,
and comes out and washes his hands.
And they bring him a handful of שתיתא made from lentils,
and a handful of aged wine,
and he should mix them together and eat it;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's mother's answer from step 16 about how אחילו is treated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How is אחילו treated? (asked in step 15)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After a full meal and a bathroom visit, eat a mix of lentil שתיתא and aged wine.

steps.title: Sleeping wrapped in a sheet after the medicine
steps.stepSummary: After eating the medicine, the sick person wraps himself in a sheet and sleeps until he wakes up on his own. When he wakes, he must take the sheet off, or the illness will come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should wrap himself in his sheet and sleep. Nobody should wake him; he should get up by himself. When he gets up, he should take the sheet off. If he does not, the illness comes back on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the treatment instructions for אחילו with what to do after taking the medicine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The treatment is not only the drink. The sleep under the sheet is part of the cure. There is also a warning: if he does not remove the sheet when he wakes, the illness returns.
steps.whatToRemember: Treating אחילו has a whole routine: take it after a meal, eat lentil שתיתא mixed with aged wine, sleep wrapped in a sheet until you wake on your own, then take the sheet off.

phrases.english: and he should wrap himself in his sheet and sleep,
and there should be no one who wakes him
until he gets up on his own;
and when he gets up, he should take the sheet off himself,
and if not, it comes back upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the treatment routine that began in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After the medicine, sleep wrapped in a sheet until waking on your own, then take the sheet off so the illness does not return.

steps.title: אליהו's advice: eat a third, drink a third, leave a third
steps.stepSummary: אליהו tells רבי נתן to fill only two-thirds of his stomach, a third with food and a third with drink, and leave a third empty, so there is room when anger fills him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו said to רבי נתן: Eat a third, drink a third, and leave a third empty. Then when you get angry, you will just reach your full amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new piece of health advice, a teaching from אליהו הנביא to רבי נתן about how much to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is no longer about אחילו. It is general advice for staying healthy. The idea is that anger also 'fills' a person, so you should leave space for it and not be full from food.

phrases.english: Elijah said to Rabbi Natan:
Eat a third and drink a third,
phrases.notes: A third of what fills you up. Fill your stomach only partly.

phrases.english: and leave a third empty;
so that when you get angry, you will reach your full.
phrases.notes: The empty third leaves room for the anger, so you don't go past full.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the specific אחילו treatment to general health advice about eating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fill only two-thirds of your stomach and leave a third empty for when you get angry.

steps.title: רבי חייא's three tips for healthy digestion
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches: to avoid intestinal illness, get used to dipping your food all year round; stop eating a meal while you still enjoy it; and don't hold back when you need to relieve yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: Someone who wants to avoid stomach illness should be used to dipping his food, in summer and winter. When you are enjoying a meal, pull your hand away from it. And don't hold yourself back when you need to go to the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching (ברייתא) from רבי חייא with three pieces of advice for healthy digestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the health theme from אליהו's advice. The second tip is like אליהו's: don't eat until you are completely full. The third tip connects to the bathroom routine in the אחילו treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: Pull your hand away, stop eating

phrases.english: Rabbi Hiyya teaches:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא לִידֵי חוֹלִי מֵעַיִים,
phrases.english: One who wants not to come to intestinal illness
should be used to dipping, summer and winter;
phrases.notes: Dipping his food, like bread, into wine or vinegar.

phrases.english: a meal that you enjoy,
pull your hand away from it;
and do not hold yourself back
at a time when you need to relieve yourself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more general health advice after אליהו's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To avoid stomach illness: dip your food all year, stop eating while you still enjoy the meal, and don't delay going to the bathroom.

steps.title: מר עוקבא: cheap white wine causes weakness
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא says that someone who drinks טיליא חיורא, a cheap white wine, will be struck by weakness.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא said: Someone who drinks cheap white wine will be seized by weakness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a warning from מר עוקבא about a harmful kind of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The health advice now turns to drinks. מר עוקבא names one kind of wine and says it causes weakness. This sets up רב חסדא's statement in the next step, which ranks the wines.

keyTerms.meaning: Seizes him, takes hold of him

phrases.english: Mar Ukva said:
This one who drinks cheap white wine,
weakness seizes him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the health advice, now about which wine is harmful.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking cheap white wine brings on weakness.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the best and worst of sixty wines
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says there are sixty kinds of wine. The best is red, fragrant wine. The worst is cheap white wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: There are sixty kinds of wine. The best of them all is red, fragrant wine. The worst of them all is cheap white wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא ranks the kinds of wine and agrees with מר עוקבא that cheap white wine is the worst.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר עוקבא only said cheap white wine is harmful. רב חסדא adds the bigger picture: out of sixty kinds, it is the very worst, and red fragrant wine is the very best.
steps.whatToRemember: Health advice in this section: don't eat until you are completely full, dip your food, don't delay the bathroom, and avoid cheap white wine. Red, fragrant wine is the best.

phrases.english: Rav Hisda said:
There are sixty kinds of wine;
the best of them all is red, fragrant wine,
the worst of them all is cheap white wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא שִׁיתִּין מִינֵי חַמְרָא הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports מר עוקבא by calling cheap white wine the worst of all wines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of sixty kinds of wine, red fragrant wine is best and cheap white wine is worst.

steps.title: Fire, oil and sun in the mornings of Nisan cause weakness
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that someone who sits by a fire on a ניסן morning, rubs himself with oil, and then goes out to sit in the sun will be struck by weakness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: If a person sits near a fire in the mornings of ניסן, rubs himself with oil, and then goes out and sits in the sun, he will become weak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of health warnings. רב יהודה describes a combination of three activities that leads to weakness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger is the combination of all three: fire, then oil, then sun. This fits the earlier steps, which also warned about things that bring on weakness, like the cheap white wine in Step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: The mornings of the month of ניסן

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
This one who sits during the mornings of Nisan
near the fire,
and rubs himself with oil,
and then goes out and sits in the sun –
weakness will seize him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הַאי מַאן דְּיָתֵיב בְּצַפְרָנֵי נִיסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another cause of weakness to the list of health warnings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sitting by a fire on a ניסן morning, rubbing with oil, and then sitting in the sun causes weakness.

steps.title: Marital relations after bloodletting harm the children
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a man lets blood and then has marital relations, his children will be weak. If both husband and wife let blood, the children will have the disease רָאתָן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: If a man had blood let and then had marital relations, he will have weak children. If both of them had blood let and then had relations, they will have children with the disease רָאתָן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that moves to a new topic: the effect of bloodletting on children conceived right afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. If only the husband let blood, the children are weak. If both parents let blood, the harm is worse: a specific disease called רָאתָן.

keyTerms.meaning: Let blood, a common medical treatment

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who let blood and then had marital relations –
will have weak children.
If both of them let blood and had relations –
they will have children afflicted with ra'atan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הִקִּיז דָּם וְשִׁימֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from general causes of weakness to harm that comes to children conceived at certain times.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations after bloodletting lead to weak children. If both parents let blood, the children will have רָאתָן.

steps.title: רב פפא limits the warning: eating something removes the danger
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the warning about bloodletting applies only if the person ate nothing afterward. If he ate something, there is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We only said this when he did not eat anything after the bloodletting. But if he ate something, there is no concern.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא narrows the ברייתא from the previous step. He tells us exactly when its warning applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sounded like relations after bloodletting are always harmful. רב פפא limits it to a case where the person has not eaten. Eating something afterward removes the danger completely.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when (a phrase that limits an earlier teaching)
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא טָעֵים מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: We said this only when he did not taste anything,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the warning about bloodletting in the ברייתא just before.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל טָעֵים מִידֵּי – לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if he tasted something – we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא טָעֵים מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא of Step 24 to a case where the person has not eaten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bloodletting warning applies only when nothing was eaten afterward. Eating removes the concern.

steps.title: Marital relations right after a journey lead to weak children
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא says that a man who comes back from a trip and has marital relations right away will have weak children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: If a man came back from traveling and had marital relations, he will have weak children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another time when marital relations are harmful: right after coming home from a journey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the bloodletting ברייתא. A man who is tired and drained, here from traveling, should not have relations right away, or the children will be weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Came back from the road, returned from a journey

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
One who came back from the road and had marital relations –
will have weak children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: בָּא מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ וְשִׁימֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another situation, coming back from a journey, that leads to weak children, like bloodletting does.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations right after returning from a journey lead to weak children.

steps.title: Wait after using the bathroom before marital relations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that after using the bathroom, a man should wait the time it takes to walk half a מיל before having relations, because the bathroom demon goes with him. If he does not wait, his children will be epileptic.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: Someone who comes from the bathroom should not have marital relations until he waits the time it takes to walk half a מיל, because the demon of the bathroom goes along with him. If he did have relations, he will have epileptic children.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא gives a rule about waiting after using the bathroom. It explains the reason and the harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step gives a rule (wait), a set amount of time (half a מיל), and a reason (the bathroom demon is still with him). The harm is worse than plain weakness: the children will be epileptic.

keyTerms.meaning: The time it takes to walk half a מיל

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who comes from the bathroom
should not have marital relations
until he waits the measure of half a mil,
phrases.notes: This is a measure of time: as long as it takes to walk half a מיל.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשֵּׁד בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא מְלַוֶּה עִמּוֹ;
phrases.english: because the demon of the bathroom accompanies him;
and if he did have relations –
he will have epileptic children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of bad times for relations, now with a set waiting time and a stated reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After using the bathroom, wait the time it takes to walk half a מיל before relations. Otherwise the children will be epileptic.

steps.title: Certain positions during marital relations harm the man
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that having relations standing brings on spasms. Sitting, or with the woman above, brings on the illness דָּלָרְיָא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One who has marital relations standing will be struck with spasms. If sitting, he will be struck with דָּלָרְיָא. If she is above and he is below, he will be struck with דָּלָרְיָא.
steps.whatsHappening: A final ברייתא lists positions that bring illness. This time the harm falls on the man himself, not on the children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step changes who is harmed. The earlier steps warned about the children, but here the man himself gets sick. Two of the three positions lead to the same illness, דָּלָרְיָא.
steps.whatToRemember: This whole section is health advice. It names times and ways of marital relations (after bloodletting without eating, after a journey, right after the bathroom, and certain positions) that the חכמים warned can harm the children or the man himself.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who has marital relations standing –
spasms will seize him;
sitting – dalarya will seize him;
she above and he below –
dalarya will seize him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from harm to the children to harm to the man himself, based on position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Standing brings spasms. Sitting, or the woman above, brings דָּלָרְיָא.

steps.title: What is the illness דלריא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the illness דלריא, mentioned in the last ברייתא, actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is דלריא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the illness named in the previous ברייתא. This sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 said that relations while sitting, or with the woman above, cause דלריא. The word is unfamiliar, so the גמרא stops to ask about it.

keyTerms.meaning: An illness, mentioned in step 28 as coming from certain positions in relations

phrases.english: What is dalarya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a term used in step 28.

steps.title: The remedy for דלריא is דרדרא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers by naming the cure for דלריא, a plant called דרדרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: the remedy for דלריא is דרדרא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי responds to the question. Instead of describing the illness, he tells us what cures it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is practical. It does not define the sickness, but it gives the medicine. This brings in a new unfamiliar word, דרדרא.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant used as the remedy

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The remedy for dalarya is dardara.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי סַם דָּלָרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question in step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cure for דלריא is דרדרא.

steps.title: What is דרדרא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks what the remedy דרדרא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is דרדרא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the new word that was just used. This sets up אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 30 used a word that also needs explaining, so the גמרא follows up right away.

phrases.english: What is dardara?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the term used in step 30.

steps.title: דרדרא is saffron of thorns
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that דרדרא is a thorny saffron plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is saffron of thorns.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי identifies the plant, so now we know what the remedy is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this answer the chain of questions is complete. דלריא is cured by דרדרא, and דרדרא is a saffron that grows among thorns.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Saffron of thorns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 31.

steps.title: How רב פפא and רב פפי took the remedy
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים used the remedy differently. רב פפא chewed it and swallowed it, and רב פפי chewed it and spat it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא would chew it and swallow it. רב פפי would chew it and spit it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how two Sages actually used this plant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report shows two ways to take the remedy. Either swallow it, or just chew it and spit it out. The גמרא does not say which way is better.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא and רב פפי are two different people with very similar names. Read carefully.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa would chew and swallow it.
Rav Pappi would chew and spit it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how the remedy from step 32 was used in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The remedy can be chewed and swallowed, or chewed and spat out.

steps.title: אביי's drink for weakness in relations
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a remedy for a man who is weak in relations: grind thorny safflower, boil it in wine, and drink it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: a man who is not strong in relations should take three measures of safflower thorns. He should grind them, boil them in wine, and drink.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new remedy, this time for a man who is weak in marital relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the remedy just discussed, since it also uses a thorny plant. The recipe has three steps: grind, boil in wine, drink.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the way of the world'. Here it is a polite term for marital relations.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One who is not expert in the way of the world,
phrases.notes: He means a man who lacks strength in marital relations.

phrases.english: let him bring three vessels of safflower thorns,
and grind them, and boil them in wine, and drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the remedy for דלריא to a related remedy for weakness in relations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Safflower thorns boiled in wine strengthen a man who is weak in relations.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: these restored my youth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that remedies like these brought back his youthful strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: these are the things that brought me back to my youth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a personal report backing up these remedies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His statement is a firsthand report that the remedies work. That gives weight to אביי's recipe.
steps.whatToRemember: The remedies section goes in order: what cures דלריא, what that plant is, how it was taken, and a drink for weakness, which רבי יוחנן says worked for him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
These are what returned me to my youth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֵן הֵן הֶחְזִירוּנִי לְנַעֲרוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's remedy with personal experience.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These remedies restore youthful strength.

steps.title: Three things weaken a person
steps.stepSummary: A new list says that fear, travel, and sin weaken a person's strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three things weaken a person's strength: fear, the road, and sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new list of three things that drain a person's strength. Proofs for each item come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the theme of strength and weakness. Step 26 warned that relations right after a journey lead to weak children. This list says outright that travel itself drains a person's strength, along with fear and sin.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַכְחִישִׁים כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Three things weaken a person's strength,
and they are: fear, the road, and sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַכְחִישִׁים כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new list on the theme of physical strength.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fear, travel, and sin weaken a person.

steps.title: Verses proving each of the three
steps.stepSummary: Each of the three items is proven from a פסוק in תהלים that links it to losing strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fear: 'My heart flutters, my strength leaves me.' The road: 'He weakened my strength on the road.' Sin: 'My strength fails because of my sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק for each item on the list to show that it weakens a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every פסוק uses the word כֹחִי, 'my strength', together with one of the three causes. This shows that the list comes from the verses themselves.

phrases.english: Fear, as it is written:
"My heart flutters, my strength fails me."
The road, as it is written:
"He has weakened my strength on the road."
Sin, as it is written:
"My strength fails because of my sin."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves each item of the list in step 36.
steps.raayaObject: That fear, travel, and sin weaken a person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Three פסוקים in תהלים, each mentioning כֹחִי.

steps.title: Three things done standing harm the body
steps.stepSummary: Eating, drinking, or having relations while standing breaks a person's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three things break a person's body: eating standing, drinking standing, and having relations standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second list of three, about actions done while standing that harm the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches step 28, which said relations while standing bring on spasms. Here standing is also harmful for eating and drinking.
steps.whatToRemember: Two lists of three. Fear, travel, and sin weaken strength. Eating, drinking, and relations while standing break the body.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַתִּיזִין גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Three things break a person's body,
and they are: one who ate standing,
and drank standing,
and had marital relations standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַתִּיזִין גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel list of three, echoing step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating, drinking, or having relations while standing harms the body.

steps.title: Five actions that bring a person closer to death
steps.stepSummary: Five actions followed by standing up right away bring a person closer to death than to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five things put a person closer to death than to life: eating and then standing up, drinking and then standing up, letting blood and then standing up, sleeping and then standing up, and having relations and then standing up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new health list: five actions that are dangerous when a person stands up right after doing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on step 38, which warned against eating, drinking, or having relations while standing. Here the danger is getting up right away after the action. The list adds two new items: letting blood and sleeping.

keyTerms.meaning: And he stood up, meaning right away after the action
Let blood, an old medical practice
Had marital relations, literally 'used his bed'

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה קְרוֹבִין לְמִיתָה יוֹתֵר מִן הַחַיִּים,
phrases.english: Five are closer to death than to life,
and these are they: he ate and stood up,
he drank and stood up, he let blood and stood up,
he slept and stood up, he had relations and stood up.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה קְרוֹבִין לְמִיתָה יוֹתֵר מִן הַחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the health warnings about standing, from step 38, with a new numbered list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating, drinking, bloodletting, sleeping, or relations followed right away by standing up put a person closer to death than to life.

steps.title: Six actions that kill a person immediately
steps.stepSummary: Six actions, done one after another, cause immediate death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Six things kill a person right away if he does them: coming back from a trip tired, letting blood, going into the bathhouse, drinking until drunk, sleeping on the ground, and having relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a stronger list: six actions that, done together, cause death right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five-item list only said a person comes 'closer to death.' This list is far more severe: the person dies right away. Each item weakens the body, and together they are deadly.

phrases.english: Six: one who does them dies immediately,
and these are they: one who came from a journey and was exhausted,
let blood, and went into the bathhouse,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁתָה וְנִשְׁתַּכֵּר, וְיָשַׁן עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע,
phrases.english: and drank and became drunk, and slept on the ground,
and had relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from five actions that bring a person close to death to six that kill outright.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who does all six of these actions dies immediately.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only when done in this order
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the six-item rule to when the actions are done in the listed order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This is only when he did them in this order.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a condition: the six actions kill right away only if they are done in the exact order listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, we might think any combination of the six is deadly. רבי יוחנן narrows the rule: the order matters. This opens the question of what happens when they are done out of order, which אביי answers next.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when, a phrase that limits a rule
In their order, the order of the list

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And this is only when he did them in their order.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְהוּא שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן כְּסִידְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to the six-item list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six actions cause immediate death only when done in the listed order.

steps.title: אביי: in order means death, out of order means weakness
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that doing the six in order kills, while doing them out of order only weakens.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If he does them in order, he dies. If not in order, he becomes weak.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי fills in what רבי יוחנן left open: what happens if the six actions are done out of order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן only said that in order is deadly. אביי adds the other side: out of order is still harmful, but it makes a person weak, not dead. So doing them out of order is not safe, just less deadly.

phrases.english: Abaye said: in their order, he dies;
not in their order, he becomes weak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the other side of רבי יוחנן's condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing the six in order kills; doing them out of order causes weakness.

steps.title: Challenge from מעורת's slave who died from three actions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: מעורת's slave died after only three of the actions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But מעורת made her slave do three of these, and he died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי with a story: a woman named מעורת had her slave do only three of the six actions, and he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that even all six out of order only cause weakness. Yet here only three caused death. That seems to show that fewer actions, not in full order, can still kill.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A word that opens a challenge
But look, here is a case

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But Me'oret made her slave do
three of them, and he died!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא מְעוּרַת עֲבַדָה לֵיהּ לְעַבְדַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's rule with a real-life case.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's statement that the actions done out of order only weaken a person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only three actions killed the slave, then a partial set, not in full order, can cause death, against אביי.

steps.title: Answer: that slave was already weak
steps.stepSummary: The slave died because he was already frail, so the case does not disprove אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That slave was weak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the slave in the story was already weak, which is why fewer actions killed him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's rule is about a normal, healthy person. A person who is already frail can die from less. So the story is an unusual case and does not break the rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The six actions kill a healthy person only in order; out of order they weaken him. A person already frail can die from fewer of them.

phrases.english: That one was weak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from מעורת's slave.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the person in the story was not healthy.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slave's death shows that three actions can kill anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slave was already frail; for a normal person אביי's rule stands.

steps.title: Eight things that are harmful in large amounts and good in small amounts
steps.stepSummary: A list of eight things that hurt in large amounts but help in small amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Eight things are hard in large amounts and good in small amounts: travel, relations, wealth, work, wine, sleep, hot water, and bloodletting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new list: eight things that are good in small doses but harmful in large doses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier lists, these are not simply dangerous. Each one is helpful in moderation and only harmful when overdone. Some items repeat earlier ones, like wine, sleep, and bloodletting, but now the point is the amount.

keyTerms.meaning: A lot of them is hard, harmful
A little of them is good
Hot water, bathing in hot water

steps.whatToRemember: These eight things, including travel, wine, sleep, and work, help in small amounts and hurt in large amounts.

phrases.english: Eight: much of them is hard, and a little of them is good,
and these are they: travel, and the way of the world,
phrases.notes: 'The way of the world' here is a polite way of saying marital relations.

phrases.english: wealth, and work, wine, and sleep,
hot water, and bloodletting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new numbered list, moving from deadly actions to things that depend on amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Travel, relations, wealth, work, wine, sleep, hot water, and bloodletting are harmful in large amounts and good in small amounts.

steps.title: Eight things that decrease fertility
steps.stepSummary: A list of eight things that decrease the זרע, with bloodletting on the lower body counted as twice as harmful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Eight things decrease a man's semen: salt, hunger, the skin disease נתק, crying, sleeping on the ground, the melilot plant, unripe dodder, and bloodletting on the lower body, which is twice as harmful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its run of medical lists with a new list of eight things that reduce a man's fertility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier list was about things whose effect depends on the amount. This list is simply about one kind of harm: weakening the זרע. The last item, הקזת דם on the lower body, is set apart as doing double damage compared to the others.

keyTerms.meaning: A skin disease of the head or beard

phrases.english: Eight things decrease the semen,
and these are they: salt, and hunger,
and netek (a skin disease), crying,
and sleeping on the ground,
and the melilot plant,
and dodder eaten not in its time,
phrases.notes: "Not in its time" means eaten before it is ripe.

phrases.english: and bloodletting below – twice as much.
phrases.notes: "Below" means on the lower part of the body. It does double the harm of the other items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another list of eight, following the list of eight in step 45.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight things reduce fertility. Bloodletting on the lower body does twice the damage.

steps.title: Bloodletting above is twice as beneficial
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that just as bloodletting below is doubly harmful, bloodletting above is doubly beneficial. Then the גמרא introduces a statement of רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: just as bloodletting on the lower body is twice as harmful, bloodletting on the upper body is twice as beneficial. רב פפא said:
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds the positive side of the last item in the list. The final words introduce רב פפא, whose statement comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list only told us that low bloodletting hurts. The ברייתא adds that the place matters in both directions: low bloodletting does double harm, and high bloodletting does double good. The words אמר רב פפא set up the next statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Below, on the lower part of the body
Above, on the upper part of the body

phrases.english: It was taught: Just as it is twice as harmful below,
so too it is twice as beneficial above.
Rav Pappa said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the last item of step 46 by giving its positive opposite, then sets up רב פפא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bloodletting on the upper body is twice as beneficial, just as bloodletting on the lower body is twice as harmful.
